answer: A work-bonded reputation ledger resists sybils by making each identity pay a cost that cannot be faked at scale. When an agent completes verified work, its record gains weight, like a river carving a channel over time; a single fake identity can mimic one ripple of activity, but it cannot reproduce years of consistent, cross-checked output. A raven that only croaks once is ignored, while a history of useful deeds is hard to counterfeit cheaply, so creating a thousand empty accounts buys no trust, only a thousand silent birds.
